children: Orthopediatrics reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $72.7M, up 18.6% from $61.3M a year earlier. Net loss narrowed to $5.9M from $11.8M, while diluted loss per share improved to $(0.25) from $(0.50).
Revenue was $72.7M, compared with $61.3M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 18.6%.
Net loss was $5.9M, compared with a net loss of $11.8M in the prior-year quarter.
Diluted EPS was $(0.25), compared with $(0.50) in the prior-year quarter.
Net revenue rose 19% in the quarter and 16% year to date, driven by Trauma and Deformity and specialty bracing. Trauma and Deformity grew 20% year to date.
Scoliosis growth was supported by VerteGlide and Response, partly offset by lower 7D unit sales.
The company began direct sales in Brazil and India, expanded its international footprint, and consolidated German warehousing in the Netherlands.
More than 60 U.S. orthotics and prosthetics clinics support growth plans that include product expansion, sales infrastructure, consigned sets, and additional clinics.
